title: Achieving Low-Latency Graph-Based Vector Search via Aligning Best-First Search Algorithm with SSD
problem: Approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search on large-scale datasets exceeds GPU/CPU memory capacity, requiring disk-based solutions that align with I/O patterns
motivation: Vector search at billion-scale is fundamental to AI systems (RAG, semantic search). Current in-memory solutions don't scale to production datasets without prohibitive memory costs
method: Best-first search algorithm optimized for SSD access patterns through I/O-aware graph traversal and prefetching strategies
key_novelty: First graph-based ANN system that efficiently exploits SSD characteristics for best-first search, achieving latency competitive with in-memory systems
contributions: Graph-based ANN algorithm tailored for SSD I/O characteristics
1.14-2.02x latency improvement vs in-memory Vamana on billion-scale datasets
35% latency of DiskANN on same datasets, indicating better algorithm efficiency
Practical solution for billion-scale vector search without massive memory
hardware_target: GPU systems with SSD backing store
limitations: Primarily disk-based, so latency higher than all in-memory systems; algorithm complexity for very dynamic workloads unclear; SSD wear patterns not discussed
